indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.1.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Know the basic structure of plants (roots, stem, leaves, flowers)

skills.description: Name the four basic parts of a plant
Identify plant parts from a picture, drawing, or real plant
State simply what each part does
Draw and label a plant showing the four basic parts

misconceptions: Roots are not part of the plant.
Flowers are only for decoration; they have no job.
The stem is just a stick; it does not carry water.
All plants have all four parts visible at all times.

questions.stem: Which part of a plant is usually under the ground?
hints: It holds the plant in the soil.
You cannot see it above the ground.
questions.explanation: The roots are the part of the plant that grows under the ground.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the stem goes all the way underground.

questions.stem: Which part of a plant is usually green and flat?
questions.explanation: Leaves are usually green and flat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse leaves with the stem.

questions.stem: What do we call the colourful part of a plant?
hints: It can be red, yellow, or pink.
questions.explanation: The flower is the colourful part of the plant.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the flower is only for looking at.

questions.stem: Which part holds the leaves up to the sun?
hints: It connects the roots to the leaves.
questions.explanation: The stem holds the plant up, including the leaves.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the roots hold the leaves up.

questions.stem: Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.explanation: The roots take in water from the soil.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the stem takes in water directly from the soil.

questions.stem: Kofi pulls a small plant from the ground. He sees a part with tiny hairs on it that was in the soil. What part is this?
questions.explanation: The part with tiny hairs that was in the soil is the root.
questions.misconception: Pupils may call it a stem because it looks like a thin stick.

questions.stem: Why do plants have leaves?
questions.explanation: Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think leaves are only for decoration.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a basic part of a plant?
questions.explanation: A stone is not a part of a plant. Roots, stems, and leaves are plant parts.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think stones are part of the plant because they are in the soil.

questions.stem: Ama sees a plant with roots, a stem, and green leaves. She does not see any flowers. Is this a plant?
options: No, it is not a plant
Yes, but it is missing a flower
hints: Does it have roots and leaves?
Can a plant live without flowers?
questions.explanation: Yes, it is still a plant. Some plants do not have flowers, or they have not grown flowers yet.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all plants must have flowers to be a plant.

questions.stem: What job does the stem do for the plant?
options: It takes in water from the soil
It carries water to the leaves
hints: It connects the roots and the leaves.
questions.explanation: The stem carries water from the roots to the leaves.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the stem only holds the plant up and does nothing else.

questions.stem: Name two parts of a plant.
hints: What is under the ground? What is green?
questions.explanation: Two parts of a plant are roots and leaves (or stem and flower).
questions.misconception: Pupils may name non-plant parts like soil.

questions.stem: What part of the plant is found under the soil?
hints: You cannot see it above the ground.
questions.explanation: The roots are found under the soil.
questions.misconception: Pupils may answer 'stem' because stems can be near the ground.

questions.stem: If you remove the roots of a plant, what will happen to the plant?
options: It will not get water and may die
It will turn into a flower
hints: Where does the plant get water?
questions.explanation: Roots take in water. Without roots, the plant cannot get water and may die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think roots are not important.

questions.stem: Kwame is drawing a plant. He draws a line going straight up from the ground. He adds leaves to the sides. What is the line he drew?
questions.explanation: The line going straight up is the stem.
questions.misconception: Pupils may call the stem a root.

questions.stem: Why does a plant need flowers?
hints: What do we plant to grow new plants?
questions.explanation: Flowers help the plant make seeds so new plants can grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think flowers are just for beauty.

questions.stem: Adwoa has a leaf and a flower. How are they different?
options: The leaf is usually green, the flower is colourful
The leaf is usually colourful, the flower is green
The leaf is under the ground
The flower is under the ground
questions.explanation: Leaves are usually green, while flowers can be many colours like red, yellow, or pink.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not have observed flowers closely.

questions.stem: Draw a plant showing the roots, stem, and one leaf. Label the three parts.
hints: Start with the root at the bottom.
Add the stem and a leaf.
questions.explanation: This tests observation and drawing of plant parts.

questions.stem: Explain why a plant is called a living thing because of its parts.

criteria.description: Mentions that it has parts that help it grow or make food
Mentions that it takes in water or air

hints: What does the plant do with its leaves?
questions.explanation: A plant is a living thing because its parts help it grow, take in water (roots), and make food (leaves).

questions.stem: Draw a flower and label it.
questions.explanation: This tests identification and drawing of the flower.

questions.stem: A plant has roots, a stem, and leaves. It does NOT have flowers. What can we say about this plant?
options: It is a plant that may not grow flowers
hints: Are roots and leaves enough to make it a plant?
Do all plants have visible flowers all the time?
questions.explanation: Not all plants have visible flowers. As long as it has roots, a stem, and leaves, it is a plant.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all plants must have flowers.
